explain.label: What is this? {title}
explain.evapotranspiration.title: Evapotranspiration (water use)
explain.evapotranspiration.body: Evapotranspiration is the water a field loses to the air: evaporation from the soil surface plus transpiration from the crop. The two happen at the same time and are hard to tell apart, so they are computed together. FieldWitness computes it from NASA POWER weather with the FAO-56 method.
explain.soil_moisture_anomaly.title: Soil-moisture anomaly
explain.soil_moisture_anomaly.body: NASA's SMAP mission monitors soil moisture from space; FieldWitness uses its root-zone estimate. The anomaly is the difference from the usual value for the same month: below zero means drier than usual. A shortage of soil moisture is what defines agricultural drought.
explain.ndvi.title: NDVI (greenness)
explain.ndvi.body: NDVI is computed from the visible and near-infrared light that plants reflect: NDVI = (NIR − VIS) / (NIR + VIS). Values of 0.1 and below mean bare ground; 0.8–0.9 means the densest green leaves. FieldWitness reads it from NASA HLS satellite images at 30 m.
explain.frost.title: Frost risk
explain.frost.body: Frost damage happens when ice forms inside the plant tissue and injures the cells: it is the ice, not the cold alone, that harms the plant. The calendar shows the share of past years in which the daily minimum temperature fell below the crop's threshold in that month.
explain.frost.source: Snyder & de Melo-Abreu (2005), Frost Protection, Vol. 1, Chapter 4 (FAO)
explain.water_balance.title: Water balance
explain.water_balance.body: The water balance tracks the water in the root zone day by day: rain and irrigation fill it, crop water use and drainage empty it. When the shortage passes the readily available water, the crop is stressed and uses less water. FieldWitness uses the FAO-56 root-zone water balance.
explain.ryi.title: Relative Yield Index
explain.ryi.body: The Relative Yield Index compares the expected yield with the yield the same crop would give without water shortage, on a 0–1 scale (1 = no loss). It uses the crop's yield response factor Ky, which describes how relative yield falls when crop water use falls short. It is not a yield in tonnes.
explain.ryi.source: FAO-56 (Allen et al. 1998), Chapter 8, Table 24 (from FAO Paper 33)
explain.evidence_grade.title: Evidence grade
explain.evidence_grade.body: A: physics and neighbouring fields agree, this field's past makes the physics credible, and no key input is an assumption. B: two witnesses agree. C: only one witness, or the witnesses disagree; D: most inputs that drive the decision are assumptions.
explain.evidence_grade.source: FieldWitness grading rules (config/grading.yaml); the thresholds are team choices, not taken from a paper
explain.source_tags.title: Source letters
explain.source_tags.body: Every number carries a letter: O = observed by satellite, D = derived by a model from satellite data, E = external data not from NASA, A = assumption. Point at a letter to see its exact source.
explain.source_tags.source: FieldWitness data rules (every number shown carries a source tag)
explain.nitrogen_fixing.title: Nitrogen-fixing crops
explain.nitrogen_fixing.body: Pulses take nitrogen from the air through biological nitrogen fixation and turn it into a form plants can use. FAO reports that pulses get over 60 % of their nitrogen this way, and promotes growing them in rotation with staple crops to enrich the soil.
explain.nitrogen_fixing.source: FAO newsroom, "Pulses and soils: a dynamic duo" (5 Feb 2024)
explain.cover_crop.title: Cover crops and ground cover
explain.cover_crop.body: Cover crops are grown in fallow periods, between the harvest of one crop and the planting of the next, using the moisture left in the soil. They protect the soil while it would otherwise be bare, including against the impact of raindrops.
explain.deep_rooting.title: Deep-rooting crops
explain.deep_rooting.body: Deep-rooting crops reach water stored lower in the soil. In the FAO-56 water balance, the water a crop can draw on grows with its rooting depth (Eq. 82), and Table 22 lists rooting depths for common crops.
explain.drought_tolerant.title: Drought tolerance and bad years
explain.drought_tolerant.body: Here a crop counts as more drought-tolerant when its yield response factor Ky is lower: its relative yield falls less when water runs short. Ky values are crop specific and may vary over the growing season. Bad-year numbers are the average of the worst 10 % of simulated weather years.
explain.root_zone_soil_water.title: Root-zone soil water
explain.root_zone_soil_water.body: The depth of water stored in the soil profile currently accessible to crop roots, expressed in millimeters. It increases when precipitation or irrigation infiltrates the ground and decreases as the crop transpires or water evaporates from the soil surface. When root-zone water falls below readily available thresholds, crop growth slows from water stress.
explain.root_zone_soil_water.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 8
explain.available_water_capacity.title: Total available water (TAW)
explain.available_water_capacity.body: The total amount of water that a soil profile can store between field capacity and wilting point within the crop root zone. It depends on soil physical texture across sand, silt, and clay fractions and deepens over the season as root depth expands. Soils with higher available water capacity buffer crops longer against dry spells between rain events.
explain.available_water_capacity.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 8
explain.water_stress_ks.title: Water stress coefficient (Ks)
explain.water_stress_ks.body: A dimensionless transpiration reduction factor between 0.00 and 1.00 calculated directly from daily root-zone soil water depletion. When available water remains above the crop depletion threshold, Ks equals 1.00 and transpiration proceeds without restriction. As soil dries past this threshold, Ks drops toward zero, causing modeled canopy greenness and water use to fade.
explain.water_stress_ks.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 8
explain.canopy_proxy.title: Canopy proxy (Kc / Kc max)
explain.canopy_proxy.body: The ratio of the crop basal crop coefficient Kc to its peak mid-season coefficient Kc max, scaled between 0.00 and 1.00. It is a simulation output tracing phenological leaf area progression across growth stages, not a direct satellite photo measurement. In the 3D scene, this proxy scales the height and density of procedural plant models.
explain.canopy_proxy.source: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Chapter 6
explain.fallow_bare_soil.title: Fallow and bare soil
explain.fallow_bare_soil.body: A fallow period leaves the field unplanted between cash crops, meaning no crop transpires and plant canopy stays at zero. While fallow conserves some moisture for subsequent planting, extended bare-soil months expose the surface to wind erosion, moisture evaporation, and organic matter loss. FieldWitness tracks bare-soil months and applies penalties to discourage uninterrupted fallow.
explain.fallow_bare_soil.source: FAO Conservation Agriculture: Soil organic cover
explain.hindcast.title: Hindcast evaluation
explain.hindcast.body: An empirical evaluation where past seasons are simulated using only data available before planting commenced. It tests model skill against actual historical satellite vegetation trajectories without looking ahead. Under SSURGO [E] soil physics, Kansas hindcasts outperformed baselines B1/B2 overall and across all 3 crops, and Phase 4 Split-CQR calibration lifted 90% coverage to 80.2–91.1% asym (86.3–91.1% sym) for start-of-season and 88.8% asym for winter-wheat cover days.
explain.crps.title: Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS)
explain.crps.body: A standard probabilistic verification metric measuring the distance between a predicted probability distribution and an observed outcome. Lower values indicate better probabilistic accuracy, with 0 representing a perfect probabilistic match. FieldWitness uses CRPS to evaluate whether ensemble simulations capture true crop canopy trajectories.
explain.credibility.title: Credibility score
explain.credibility.body: A composite confidence metric assessing whether local data supports a field simulation. It checks satellite observation density, model-observation agreement, and environmental plausibility. Fields with low credibility are flagged or capped at lower evidence grades.
explain.witness.title: Witness system
explain.witness.body: The three-way verification framework in FieldWitness: physics simulation (Witness 1), past field history (Witness 2), and causal neighbour contrasts (Witness 3). In Kansas, Witness 3 is kept strictly OFF because no contrast passed causal balance diagnostics; in Central Ukraine (T36UVU), Panel-OBDML and Exact-Year DAPSM pass 30 pre-cutoff checks and are active (tag D).
explain.bare_soil_months.title: Bare-soil months
explain.bare_soil_months.body: The cumulative number of months in a multi-year rotation where ground cover remains below protective thresholds. Extended bare soil leaves agricultural land vulnerable to wind erosion, organic matter depletion, and evaporation. The ranking engine penalizes excessive bare-soil months to favor soil-conserving rotations.
explain.bare_soil_months.source: FAO Conservation Agriculture: Soil organic cover
explain.bad_year_water.title: Bad-year water use
explain.bad_year_water.body: The modeled crop evapotranspiration during the driest historical weather year in the field record. It reveals how severely water demand and stress escalate when precipitation fails. Adjusting the bad-year water priority slider favors crop rotations that remain resilient under drought.
explain.plain_summary.title: Plain-language summary
explain.plain_summary.body: This summary compares your current rotation against the highest-ranked alternative under your active priorities and constraints. Differences below set thresholds are called about the same, and opposing changes are shown as trade-offs. Every water and bare-soil figure carries a provenance letter and links back to its model evidence.
explain.pareto_ranking.title: Pareto ranking and priority weights
explain.pareto_ranking.body: Options are scored from 0 to 1 on each criterion relative to the other rotations simulated for this field. Each normalised score is multiplied by your chosen priority weight and summed into a total weighted score. Moving any slider updates the order live without inventing hidden bonuses.
explain.weather_whatif.title: Weather what-if scenarios
explain.weather_whatif.body: Weather what-ifs perturb the historical meteorological record by fixed steps in temperature and rainfall. They test how sensitive a rotation ranking is to warmer or drier seasons rather than predicting future climate. A robust option stays competitive across both normal and stressed weather steps.
explain.regret.title: Decision regret
explain.regret.body: Regret measures how much an option falls short of the best-performing rotation in each simulated past weather year. Lower regret means the rotation rarely performs badly even when seasonal weather surprises the plan. Because it uses the same unit as the Relative Yield Index, regret does not predict harvest tonnage or profit.
explain.flip_probability.title: Decision flip probability
explain.flip_probability.body: Flip probability shows how often the top-ranked option changes when uncertain soil and model parameters vary across calibrated posterior worlds. A high chance means a missing local measurement—such as soil water capacity—could reverse the recommendation. Collecting that measurement narrows the uncertainty before committing to a change.
explain.root_depth.title: Effective rooting depth
explain.root_depth.body: Rooting depth traces how far down a crop extracts stored soil moisture during the season, increasing from planting to mid-season peak. Deeper roots tap a larger reservoir of available water capacity in Equation 82 of FAO-56. Shallow-rooted crops or fallow periods cannot use moisture stored below the topsoil layer.
explain.diagnosis.title: Exploratory hindcast diagnosis
explain.diagnosis.body: The diagnostic breakdown separates overall hindcast scores by crop, year, field size, evidence grade, and satellite observation count. Inference uses 1,000 spatial block bootstrap resamples across 10 km blocks so nearby fields do not inflate confidence. Groups smaller than 20 field-seasons are withheld as too few to judge.
explain.global_eval.title: Global live climate and FAO-56 evaluation
explain.global_eval.body: When a field lies outside the 320 precomputed pilot packs (200 in Kansas, 120 in Central Ukraine), FieldWitness queries multi-year daily weather from NASA POWER and soil properties from USDA SSURGO or ISRIC SoilGrids. Your browser then executes the daily FAO-56 root-zone water balance for adapted rotations using your irrigation budget and crop exclusions. Because there is no multi-year local satellite calibration here, results remain an uncalibrated baseline estimate.
explain.compare_fields.title: Side-by-side field comparison
explain.compare_fields.body: The comparison view aligns two parcels on field size, satellite observation density, calibration credibility, and rotation metrics. It computes simple B minus A deltas under default priorities so advisors can see how soil, geometry, or management alter trade-offs. Comparing two fields still reflects simulated pilot data and does not replace on-farm soil sampling.

methods.heading: Methods & Overview
methods.demo: This copy of the app runs on synthetic demo data. The methods below describe how real field packs are made.
methods.how.1: Physics: a FAO-56 root-zone water balance, driven by NASA POWER weather, simulates each rotation option on this field.
methods.how.2: Own past: the field's HLS satellite history (30 m, from 2013) calibrates the physics and gives a credibility score.
methods.how.3: Neighbours: similar fields that already grew a crop act as natural experiments for the effect of the previous crop.
methods.how.4: Agreement between the three witnesses sets an evidence grade from A to D; the options are ranked by your priorities and limits.
methods.how.5: Every recommendation is a prediction. The hindcast froze all data on 31 Dec 2021, predicted 2022–2024 and scored the predictions against what the satellite saw, next to simpler baselines (see the scoreboard).
methods.not.1: It does not predict yield in tonnes. It shows a Relative Yield Index from 0 to 1.
methods.not.2: It does not measure soil fertility from space.
methods.not.3: It does not forecast prices or profit.
methods.not.4: No language model makes the decision; the ranking is computed from the numbers shown.
methods.not.5: Weather what-ifs are sensitivity tests on past weather, not climate projections.
methods.limits.1: Coarse data (POWER weather, SMAP, GRACE, SoilGrids) is regional context or model input only. Field-level statements use HLS at 30 m from interior pixels; a source is flagged as coarse when one pixel is larger than a quarter of the field.
methods.limits.2: Field boundaries come from recent editions (CSB 2017–2024, Fields of the World 2024–25) that use imagery from after the hindcast cut-off. They are used as geometry only: no later crop labels or outcomes enter the hindcast.
methods.limits.3: Season detection upgraded via Phase 1–P2 algorithms (240 held-out Kansas field-seasons across 30 spatial blocks): TWDTW reaches 86.7 % season match (72.5 % multi-class, 90.0 % fallow), Standard DTW reaches 88.7 % binary match, WDDTW achieves 75.4 % multi-class (93.3 % fallow), and CropFormer runs in 1.05 ms/field (75.8 % multi-class, 86.7 % match; >11× faster than Savitzky–Golay), approaching the pre-registered 90.0 % target (results/story/phenology_benchmark.json).
methods.limits.4: Neighbour witness policy by region: in Kansas, Witness 3 is kept strictly OFF because 0 of 92 primary, 0 of 32 matched, and 0 of 4 DAPSM contrasts passed all diagnostic checks due to rotational confounding, so Kansas evidence grades top out at B (even with observed SSURGO 0–135 cm TAW [E] across 198 fields + SoilGrids [E] fallback on 2 shallow fields, because sowing dates still carry team-choice tag [A]). In Central Ukraine (T36UVU), pre-registered Panel-OBDML and Exact-Year DAPSM pass 30 pre-cutoff (≤ 2021) and 70 full-period contrasts (WorldCereal 2021 cropland 98.25 %, winter-wheat–maize confusion 0.0 %, maize-vs-sunflower κ = 0.035), unlocking Grades A–C (0 A / 73 B / 47 C top; 44 A among 960 candidate options across 6 crops) alongside SoilGrids 0–135 cm TAW [E] and ABC calibration (73/120 ≥ 0.60).
methods.limits.5: Hindcast calibration & skill: on 2022–2024 Kansas seasons (cut-off 2021-12-31, n = 463 across maize, sorghum & winter wheat under SSURGO [E] TAW), raw model 90 % coverage was underconfident (28.5 % canopy integral, 5.8 % cover days; Spearman ρ = 0.262). Phase 4 Split-CQR recalibration lifted 90 % coverage to 80.2–91.1 % asym (86.3–91.1 % sym) for start-of-season, 77.4–88.8 % asym (81.5–95.9 % sym) for cover days, and 71.8–79.0 % sym for canopy integral (reducing Winkler interval scores up to 78 %). In Central Ukraine (T36UVU, n = 329 field-seasons, 2022–2024), FieldWitness beats B0/B1/B2 on SOS (CRPS 12.2 vs 18.1/15.7/13.4 d), peak (14.7 vs 18.3/23.6/17.5 d), and canopy-integral rank correlation (ρ = 0.247 vs 0.185/0.203/0.150), while trailing B0 on canopy-integral CRPS (14.8 vs 13.2) and cover-days CRPS (44.6 vs 40.1 d).
methods.limits.6: Grading thresholds are team choices, marked as assumptions (A), and every change is logged in DECISIONS.md.
methods.limits.7: We could not show that evidence grades predict accuracy (n = 463 field-seasons): grade-B fields had lower average error than grade-D (CRPS 17.9 vs 24.8), but the difference is within the uncertainty (95% CI of the difference −1.5 to 13.9). Grade D had only 25 field-seasons.
methods.limits.8: Baseline comparisons evaluate all 463 paired seasons (maize, sorghum, winter wheat) and exclude fallow (not scored). Under SSURGO [E] soil physics, FieldWitness beats baselines B1 and B2 overall (CRPS 17.86 vs 19.67 / 20.45) and across every crop individually. Winter wheat exhibits a peak timing offset of about 30.0 days late (absolute error 56.0 d; proposed explanation, not tested: phenology prior stage lengths require calibration).
methods.enhancements.heading: Algorithmic enhancements benchmark (Phase 1 & Phase 4)
methods.enhancements.intro: Pre-registered Phase 1–P2 remote-sensing phenology benchmark across 240 held-out Kansas field-seasons (30 disjoint 10 km blocks; HLS tile T14SLH), replacing legacy Savitzky–Golay polynomial smoothing:
methods.enhancements.cqrSummary: Phase 4 Split-CQR recalibration (2022–2024 held-out forecast mode, 109 spatial blocks, n_cal = 3,424, n_test = 3,704) keeps point medians unchanged while lifting 90 % coverage under SSURGO [E] TAW: Start of Season 86.3–91.1 % sym / 80.2–91.1 % asym (maize 33.1→91.1 %, sorghum 64.1→89.4 %, winter wheat 18.8→86.3 % sym / 80.2 % asym), Cover Days 81.5–95.9 % sym / 77.4–88.8 % asym (wheat 3.1→88.8 % asym, Winkler 831.8→246.2), and Canopy Integral 71.8–79.0 % sym (Winkler reduced 36–64 %; max overall Winkler cut 78 % on wheat SOS). Phase P2 covariate-stratified Split-CQR (SSURGO TAW median 282.0 mm & pre-cutoff vigor) further edges asym 90 % coverage to 92.7 % maize / 90.8 % sorghum / 83.2 % wheat (SOS) and 90.4 % wheat cover days.
methods.soil.heading: Independent soil check (USDA SSURGO)
methods.soil.intro: We compared the soil water Kansas uses with an independent survey: USDA SSURGO soil maps, read at the centre of each of the 200 Kansas pilot fields (198 had a value). Both are expressed as millimetres of plant-available water over the same 0–135 cm root zone (maize roots, FAO-56 Table 22). In Central Ukraine (where SSURGO does not cover), the pipeline replaces the fixed baseline with ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 0–135 cm Saxton & Rawls (2006) TAW [E].
methods.soil.1: Independent check vs production upgrade: against the earlier 150 mm [A] baseline (sim median 142 mm), SSURGO reported nearly twice the water (median 282.1 mm, mean difference −119.3 mm, median −128 mm, n = 198). In Phase P1 (E1.2), Kansas packs switched to observed SSURGO 0–135 cm AWS [E] on 198 fields + SoilGrids 2.0 Saxton & Rawls [E] fallback on the 2 shallow fields.
methods.soil.2: Field-to-field differences do not match: Pearson r = −0.09, Spearman rho = −0.12. The fitted water capacity per field does not follow the soil survey (note that SSURGO itself varies little here: 80 % of fields lie between 230 and 295 mm).
methods.soil.3: Root-zone TAW by region: Kansas (T14SLH) now uses observed USDA-NRCS SSURGO 0–135 cm TAW [E] (198 fields, median 282.1 mm) with SoilGrids 2.0 [E] fallback (149.8 mm & 187.1 mm) on 2 shallow fields. In Central Ukraine (T36UVU), packs compute 0–135 cm TAW directly from SoilGrids 2.0 via Saxton & Rawls (191.5–241.3 mm, median 206.5 mm [E]).
methods.soil.4: SoilGrids texture vs SSURGO over the same depth: sand agrees moderately (r = 0.65, mean difference −0.7 points, MAE 7.2), clay weakly (r = 0.32, SoilGrids +6.0 points higher on average, MAE 6.3). Two fields had no SSURGO value: their soil profile ends at 91–102 cm, above the root zone.

methods.builder.heading: Rotation Builder and Farm view
methods.builder.intro: In Field in 3D you can build a three-season rotation and watch it grow next to the current one on an illustrated farm. It changes no recommendation, grade or number.
methods.builder.1: Only the field's ranked candidate rotations can be built (up to 36 in Kansas; 8 across 6 crops in Central Ukraine) following the ranking rules: at least one harvested crop, no two non-crop seasons in a row, at most two seasons of one plant family. A disabled crop card says which rule it breaks.
methods.builder.2: The table (water use, bad-year water, bare-soil months, evidence grade) comes from the ranking in the field pack, over all weather years. The 3D replay is the same FAO-56 water balance as the 3D packs, re-run in your browser for one median-rain year in normal, dry or hot weather; it matched the Python model within 0.00001 mm (20 fields × 36 rotations × 3 weathers).
methods.builder.3: The farm is an illustration of simulated values, not a photo. The barn, trees, pond, fences and paths are scenery, not data. Soil X-ray shows the same week as the glass soil view.
methods.builder.4: Limits: a season the model does not simulate (for example perennial forage in the field's history) is shown as "not simulated"; cover-crop weeks are recognised from the canopy proxy; the 3D replay is one weather year, not a forecast; it was tested with software rendering, not on every phone.
methods.wrong.heading: What we got wrong (and what changed)
methods.wrong.1: Upgraded season extraction beyond Savitzky–Golay: Initial polynomial smoothing struggled with winter wheat dormancy and fallow weeds. Replaced in Phase 1–P2 benchmarks with TWDTW (86.7 % season match, 72.5 % multi-class), Standard DTW (88.7 % binary), WDDTW (75.4 % multi-class, 93.3 % fallow), and CropFormer (75.8 % multi-class, 1.05 ms/field, >11× faster) (results/story/phenology_benchmark.json, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.2: Neighbour witness failed all diagnostics: Causal Double Machine Learning on previous-crop contrasts failed covariate balance across historical sequences and failed negative control checks (0 of 92 primary contrasts in results/neighbours/diagnostics.md, 0 of 32 in results/neighbours/matching_diagnostics.md). Kept strictly OFF in grading as an automated AI safety circuit breaker against rotational confounding; evidence grades capped at B (DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.3: Ranking rewarded fallow: Early ranking iterations scored bare fallow as optimal because it consumed zero crop transpiration, ignoring soil degradation. Fixed by introducing bare-soil month penalties and crop diversity constraints (config/ranking.yaml, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.4: Rank-order bug in packs and mis-tracked T6.8 metrics: In commit ce69ebf, packs had rank indices assigned prior to constraint filtering, and manual audit revealed T6.8 metric counts were tracked from intermediate script output. Corrected and covered with automated pack assertions (commit ce69ebf, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.5: Broken DOIs in data documentation: Automated link validation detected malformed and unreachable DOI URLs in early drafts of DATA.md. Replaced with verified persistent identifiers from official NASA DAAC and ISRIC registries (DATA.md, DECISIONS.md).
methods.wrong.6: Invented endpoints removed, verified surveys retained: Early AI exploration proposed unverified soil endpoints, which were purged in Gate 0. In Phase P1, verified USDA-NRCS SSURGO Soil Data Access (0–135 cm AWS, 198/200 Kansas fields) and ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 (250 m) were integrated with persistent provenance checks.
methods.wrong.7: Circularity trap avoided in grade validity: Evaluating whether evidence grades predicted accuracy using current grades (derived with 2022–2024 data) would have caused outcome leakage. Caught during pre-registration and strictly evaluated against cut-off grades frozen as_of(2021-12-31) (DECISIONS.md, commit e021f3e).
methods.wrong.8: Reconciled grade counts between pages: Grade B field-seasons differed between grade validity (n = 170) and diagnostic breakdowns (n = 97) because exploratory diagnostics dropped rows without baseline runs. Fixed to evaluate the full cohort across all pages (results/hindcast/diagnosis.md, scripts/t7_diagnosis.py).
methods.wrong.9: Performance regression measured, not assumed: Adding 3D simulation and guided tour caused initial Lighthouse desktop score to drop from 88 to 31 (LCP 9.7 s). Instead of assuming test machine jitter, performance tracing identified eager bundle imports; resolved via dynamic code-splitting (commit 0662f39, DECISIONS.md).
methods.roadmap.gates: Before expanding to new areas, FieldWitness tests three strict validation gates:
methods.roadmap.gate.1: 1. Census & scale gate: Field size and interior-pixel share (>= 4 interior 30 m pixels with a 15 m buffer) to prevent mixed-boundary pixel pollution.
methods.roadmap.gate.2: 2. Season detection gate: Target was 90 % accuracy against ground data. Phase 1 TWDTW reached 86.7 % season match (88.7 % DTW binary, 75.4 % WDDTW multi-class, 93.3 % fallow) and CropFormer reached 75.8 % multi-class (1.05 ms/field) across 240 held-out Kansas field-seasons. In Central Ukraine, WorldCereal / ogh-ghlc10 cross-check confirmed 98.25 % cropland and 0.0 % wheat–maize confusion; Phase P2 MAE-pretrained S2 CropFormer (0.24 ms/field) lifted Red-Edge/SWIR multi-class consistency to 85.9 % (vs 82.4 % 3-band) and pooled WorldCereal κ from 0.025 to 0.122 (92.2 % acc; 2021 8ch κ = 0.177, 94.2 % acc), while strict pre-2021->2022–2024 holdout κ stays low at 0.028 due to scarce pre-cutoff maize positives.
methods.roadmap.gate.3: 3. Hindcast & calibration gate: Split-CQR (Phase 4) lifted 90 % coverage to 86.3–91.1 % sym / 80.2–91.1 % asym (SOS) and 88.8 % asym (wheat cover days) in Kansas under SSURGO [E] TAW, while Witness 3 remains OFF (capped at B). In Central Ukraine (T36UVU, n = 329), Panel-OBDML + SoilGrids 0–135 cm TAW + 120-field ABC calibration passed causal diagnostics (30 pre-cutoff contrasts), unlocking Grades A–C across 6 crops (44 A options) and beating B0/B1/B2 on SOS & peak timing while trailing B0 on canopy integral & cover days.
methods.roadmap.privacy: Privacy & data protection: Farm locations and management practices are sensitive. In version 0 ('Add my field'), all data is stored strictly on your local device. Nothing is uploaded to any server. A future server pipeline would process and store data only with explicit user consent.
methods.roadmap.future.1: Arabic interface (i18n / RTL) for regional accessibility — shipped with 100 % bilingual parity.
methods.roadmap.future.2: Compare two fields side by side to evaluate rotations, water demand, and evidence grades across parcels — shipped across both Kansas and Ukraine.
methods.roadmap.future.3: Independent root-zone soil water and rainfall cross-checks — ERA5 0.25° extreme rain [E] wired into all 320 field calendars (SMAP & Earthdata GPM awaiting local credentials).
methods.roadmap.future.4: Evapotranspiration & surface-heat checks — Landsat 8/9 C2 L2 LST (> 35 °C) [O] wired into field calendars (ECOSTRESS v003 & Kansas WIMAS awaiting local credentials).
methods.roadmap.future.5: Expanding coverage tile-by-tile to further agricultural regions once the pre-registered validation gates pass.

advisor.caveats.season.body: Phase 1 TWDTW reached 86.7 % season match (88.7 % DTW binary; WDDTW 75.4 % multi-class, 93.3 % fallow; CropFormer 1.05 ms/field, 75.8 % multi-class) across 240 held-out Kansas field-seasons vs the 90.0 % target.
diagnosis.heading: Where it works and where it doesn't (exploratory)
diagnosis.intro: Pre-registered diagnostic evaluation (commit e021f3e, cut-off 31 Dec 2021). All statistical inference uses 1,000 spatial block bootstrap resamples across 10 km grid cells (seed 42). Any group with n < 20 is reported as "too few to judge".
diagnosis.primaryHeading: Primary Pre-Registered Question: Does FieldWitness beat Baselines B1 & B2?
diagnosis.primaryNote: Target: forecast-mode canopy-integral CRPS across all 463 paired seasons (maize, sorghum, winter wheat; fallow not scored). Success rule: the 95% spatial block bootstrap CI of the paired difference strictly excludes 0 in FieldWitness's favour.
diagnosis.expNote: All comparisons below are exploratory. Cells with n < 20 are labelled "too few to judge".
diagnosis.finding.crop.text: Skill is highest (lowest CRPS) for sorghum (CRPS 12.70, 95% CI [10.58, 15.16]), followed by maize (CRPS 18.23, 95% CI [15.99, 20.72]), and lowest for winter wheat (CRPS 21.36, 95% CI [19.39, 23.50]).
diagnosis.finding.year.text: Skill is higher in 2024 (CRPS 16.32, 95% CI [14.21, 18.49]) than in 2023 (CRPS 18.75, 95% CI [16.25, 21.63]) and 2022 (CRPS 19.31, 95% CI [16.87, 21.73]), though intervals overlap.
diagnosis.finding.field_size.text: Skill is comparable across all field size classes (<10 ha: CRPS 20.28, 95% CI [16.95, 23.93]; 10–50 ha: CRPS 16.45, 95% CI [14.44, 18.30]; >50 ha: CRPS 17.69, 95% CI [15.78, 19.72]).
diagnosis.finding.grade.text: Evidence Grade B exhibits average CRPS of 17.93 [15.55, 20.43] vs Grade C of 17.25 [15.62, 18.76] and Grade D of 24.81 [16.80, 30.85], with overlapping spatial bootstrap uncertainty.
diagnosis.finding.crop_timing_anomaly.te: Winter wheat displays a severe timing error (peak timing absolute error 56.0 d, 95% CI [48.6, 63.9] d; median signed timing error +30.0 d).
diagnosis.finding.crop_timing_anomaly.ca: Proposed explanation (not tested): Predicted peak DOY is systematically ~30 days later than observed heading in Kansas (late May vs July model peak). Phenology prior stage lengths for winter wheat require calibration (proposed as a separate decision).
diagnosis.finding.hls_observations.text: All 463 Kansas field-seasons had >=20 clear HLS observations (bins <10 and 10–19 had n=0, too few to judge).
diagnosis.finding.hls_observations.cause: Semi-arid clear skies and dual Sentinel-2 / Landsat coverage over tile T14SLH produced dense time series across all fields.

score.cqr.note: Start of Season passes 85–95 % on maize & sorghum (89.4–91.1 %; winter wheat 86.3 % sym / 80.2 % asym) and winter-wheat cover days reaches 88.8 % asym (Winkler drops from 831.8 to 246.2). Canopy integral rises from 23.4–37.3 % to 71.8–79.0 % sym (Winkler reduced 36–62 %) while missing the strict 85–95 % gate. Phase P2 covariate stratification (SSURGO TAW & pre-cutoff vigor) improves asym coverage on wheat cover days (90.4 %) and SOS (92.7 % maize, 90.8 % sorghum, 83.2 % wheat).
